overtime.title: Overtime
overtime.description: Time worked after the scheduled exit. One row per person in the period.
overtime.totalsNote: The totals above cover the full period (everyone matching the filter), not just this page.

help.title: How to read this report?
help.intro: Each row is one person in the period. The totals above sum everyone matching the filter, not just this page.
help.extra: Time worked after the scheduled exit, minus the exit tolerance. It only counts if it reaches the minimum configured in the schedule (60 min by default); above the minimum, exact minutes are counted. Clocking in early does not generate overtime.
help.worked: Total time on site (entry to exit). Includes meals and breaks.
help.scheduled: Hours set by the schedule on days the person did clock in. That's why it can be less than hours worked.
help.daysWithExtra: Number of days in the period with overtime. Not the number of clock-ins.
help.noSchedule: The person has no schedule assigned in the period, so no overtime is calculated.
help.missing: Difference when the person worked less than scheduled. Included in the CSV, not in the table.
help.restDay: If they clock in on a rest day, all time worked counts as overtime, as long as it reaches the schedule's minimum.
help.scope: The report only includes people with at least one clock-in in the period.
help.dash: “—” means there was no overtime in the period.

roster.gridIntro: Pick a shift with the brush and click cells to paint them. Use it for one-by-one adjustments.

help.title: How does it work?
help.subtitle: Weekly roster: set each person's shift, day by day.
help.baseText: Example: Ana works Housekeeping. If you change nothing, that is her assignment every week.
help.overTitle: What you change in the roster
help.overText: Example: on Sunday the 22nd Ana has a day off. That day replaces her base; the rest of the week does not change.
help.howIntro: Example: cover a 12 h guard shift on Saturday for two people.
help.step2: Select the shift in the palette. For example, "Guard (12 h)".
help.step3: Click the cells of those people on Saturday. Each cell is painted at once and marked in yellow.
help.step5: Save. If you make a mistake before saving, use Undo or Discard.
help.howNote: For changes affecting many people or days, use the "Bulk assign" mode.
help.err1: Editing the wrong week. Always check the date range above before painting.
help.err2: Forgetting to save. Pending changes are lost if you leave without saving.
help.err3: Thinking the base schedule changed. A day shift only affects that date.
help.err4: Clearing a day and not seeing the base. To go back to the base on a day, use "Base schedule" in the brush.
help.brush: The brush paints the cells you click or drag over. Shortcuts: click a person's name to fill their week; click a day header to fill that column.
help.baseConcept: "Base schedule" removes that day's shift and the person goes back to their usual schedule. Dashed cells show the base.
help.bulkStep1: Pick the shift to assign (or Day off / Base schedule).
help.bulkStep2: Mark one or more days; "Whole week" marks them all.
help.bulkStep3: Mark the people. The department filter above is respected.
help.bulkApply: Does not save: it writes the changes to the grid. Review them there and press Save.
